title: How to Choose Carpet From Samples at Home: The Mobile Showroom Method
meta: Choose carpet from samples at home by laying them flat in your light, folding them, and testing them with pets and spills. Wills Flooring's Seattle method.
keywords: how to choose carpet from samples, carpet samples at home, mobile flooring showroom Seattle, how to pick carpet color, choosing carpet Seattle

blocks.lead: Lay every sample flat on the floor of the room it is for, look at it in morning light, evening light and lamp light, then fold it, walk on it and rub it with the dog. Whatever still looks right after all that is your carpet.
blocks.detail: Carpet chosen under showroom lights comes back looking two shades different in a Seattle living room. That is the whole reason our showroom is a van. Here is the method we use on every in-home visit.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread asks why carpet always looks darker and grayer once it is installed than it did in the store. It is not the carpet, it is the light. A Ballard bedroom facing north under a February sky has nothing in common with a lit showroom, and a Capitol Hill condo with one window gets even less. Choosing at home fixes that, but only if you do it properly.

blocks.text: Step one: get the right samples into the house

items.title: Six to ten, not thirty
items.text: More than ten samples on the floor and you stop seeing them. Narrow by fiber and pile for the room first, then bring a spread of tones. We pre-sort on the van before we ring the bell.

items.title: Big enough to matter
items.text: A two-inch swatch tells you nothing. Samples should be at least a foot square so you can see the pattern repeat and the way the pile shades in different directions.

items.title: Bring the pad too
items.text: A carpet sample sitting on hardwood feels nothing like the same carpet on the pad you will actually get. We lay the pad under the sample so the step is honest.

items.title: Every room it is going in
items.text: The same oatmeal carpet reads warm in a south-facing Queen Anne bedroom and gray in the basement. If it is going in three rooms, look at it in all three.

blocks.text: Step two: the light test, three times

head: Light
What to look for
Seattle note
rows: The truest color. Does it read warm or cool next to the wall paint and trim?
North-facing rooms in Wallingford and Green Lake never get direct sun; this is as bright as it gets.
Undertones show up. Beiges turn pink, grays turn blue or green.
Winter afternoons end at 4 p.m. Half your year is this light.
Warm bulbs push everything yellow. Check that the carpet does not go muddy.
Condos with few windows live under this light most of the day.
Set the sample at the doorway where it will meet hardwood or vinyl plank.
Old fir floors in Craftsman homes are orange. Pick a carpet that flatters them.
blocks.note: Leave the samples overnight. Most people change their first choice by the next morning.

items.html: The fold, or grin, test. Bend the sample backward with the pile facing out. If you see a lot of backing between the tufts, the carpet is thin and will mat in a hallway.
Walk on it in socks and in shoes. On the pad, next to the bed where your feet land first. Plush feels great there; loop feels firm. Decide with your feet.
Rub it with the pet. Drag the sample across the dog or the cat's bed. Some fibers release hair with a shake; others hold it like Velcro.
Drip water on it. A few drops. Does it bead and wipe up, or soak in? That is the difference between a stain and a paper towel.
Brush the pile both ways. Cut-pile carpets shade: the same color looks lighter or darker by direction. If that bothers you on a sample, it will bother you across a room.
Press a wet thumb, then vacuum. Cheap fiber crushes and stays crushed. Good nylon and triexta spring back. Thirty seconds, years of regret saved.

blocks.text: Mistakes that make people regret their carpet

a.title: Choose like a pro
items: Samples flat on the floor, pad underneath
Check at three times of day, then sleep on it
Match the undertone of the wall paint and adjoining floor
Pick one shade darker than you think for halls and stairs

items: Deciding from a photo or a two-inch swatch
Holding samples vertically against a wall
Choosing a pale hallway color with a dog and two kids

blocks.title: Honest note on color:
blocks.text: Carpet installed across a whole room reads about a shade lighter and a touch more saturated than the sample on the floor, because there is more of it and it reflects on itself. If you are torn between two, take the slightly darker or grayer one.

items.html: Open the blinds and turn on the lamps you actually use. Test both.
Have paint chips or a cushion from the room nearby. Undertones either fight or agree; there is no neutral.
Have the pets home. The hair test is real.
Do the fold test on every sample before you fall in love with a color. Our guide to carpet fibers explains what the fold is telling you.
Ask to keep the top two overnight. Any company that will not leave samples is selling, not helping.
Get the pad, seams and removal on the quote. The sample is the fun part; the quote is what you live with. See how the visit works on our carpet installation page.

faq.q: Why does carpet look different at home than in the store?
faq.a: Store lighting is bright, even and usually cool white. A Seattle living room is dimmer, warmer at night and gray by day, and the carpet sits next to your walls and floors instead of other carpet. Samples laid flat at three times of day remove the surprise.

faq.q: How many carpet samples should I look at?
faq.a: Six to ten, chosen after you have narrowed the fiber and pile for the room. Looking at thirty colors at once makes them all blur together. Narrow to two, keep those overnight, and decide in the morning.

faq.q: Should I pick carpet lighter or darker than the sample?
faq.a: Assume the installed room will read a shade lighter and slightly more saturated than the sample. If you are between two, pick the darker or grayer one. For hallways and stairs in a busy Seattle household, go one shade darker than your instinct anyway.

faq.q: Does the mobile showroom cost anything?
faq.a: No. The in-home visit with samples, measuring and a written quote is free and carries no obligation. The labor side is published anyway, at $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in and $30 a step, so the visit is really about seeing the carpet in your own light and pricing the material.

faq.q: Can I keep the samples for a few days?
faq.a: Yes. We leave the finalists overnight or over a weekend so you can see them in every light and with the family walking on them. Most people change their first pick at least once, which is exactly why we do it.

faq.q: What if I like a carpet that fails the fold test?
faq.a: Use it in a low-traffic bedroom where the thin construction will not show, or find the same color in a denser line, which nearly always exists. We would rather steer you to the dense version than install something that mats in a hallway within two years.
